Generated by `modelspec-docs` from [`benchmarks/runs.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/benchmarks/runs.yaml), which holds every benchmark run measured so far: one entry per run, with the µs per step of each repeat where its source recorded them, their median, and the verification report or CHANGELOG release that states them. Each entry is validated against the JSON Schema of `modelspec.benchmark.BenchmarkRun` ([`spec/domains/benchmark.yaml`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/spec/domains/benchmark.yaml)), and a median that is not the median of its repeats is refused. Lower is faster; the charts are log scale. GPU clocks were not locked and several runs shared a loaded workstation: the `note` of each entry says how.

## MNIST 784-64-10

`mnist-784-64-10`: the median µs per step of each run over the date it ran, ModelSpec solid with filled circles and the opponents dashed with open squares. A side's runs on one date are spread across that date in the order of the file, and each ModelSpec point carries its release. An opponent's last run is carried to the right edge as a dotted line, the figure ModelSpec is measured against until that opponent is measured again.

## MLP 784-H-10 sweep

`mlp-784-H-10`: per batch, the median µs per step of the latest run at each hidden width H, ModelSpec solid with filled circles and the opponents dashed with open squares.

### Against FLOP per step

![MLP 784-H-10 sweep: µs per step against FLOP per step at batches 100, 1000 and 8192, both axes log scale](/img/benchmarks/mlp-784-h-10-flop.svg)

Every batch and hidden width in one chart: the median µs per step of each side's latest run at each point that states its FLOP per step, against that FLOP per step, both axes log scale. A side's points of one batch are joined by a line of their own, which the legend names by side and batch. The points count FLOP by `MatmulOnly`, 3196·B·H, the matmuls of a 784 → H → 10 step at batch B. The tables below give each run's GFLOP/s; [Every run](#every-run) names the source of each.

## BERT-tiny pre-training, time to the held-out baseline

`bert-tiny-pretrain`: `examples/bert_tiny.mspec` pre-trained by each side from the same initial weights on the same batches of the same packed corpus, with the same optimizer and schedule, until its held-out loss, evaluated every `Eval every` steps, is at most the target loss. Steps to target is the first evaluated step at or below the target, training seconds to target the training time up to that step without the held-out evaluations, checkpoint writes or events. µs per step is a run's training seconds over its steps, the mean of its steps, and the figure is the median of 3 runs, the median of the run's repeats as for every workload; tokens per second is its tokens per step · 10⁶ / µs per step, GFLOP/s its FLOP per step / µs per step / 1000. Each figure links to the report that states it. FLOP are counted by `MatmulOnly`, 1,170,210,816·B, the matrix products of a pre-training step, the two encoder layers, the MLM transform and the tied decoder, forward and backward, at a batch of B sequences of 128.
